comment: Mado District I (마도 Ⅰ지구, 18-1/18-2구역), 2018 excavation, same source report as mado_report_environment_v1 (Mado District II). A genuinely different real site, not a copy: real center N36 41 23.8 E126 07 41.4 (18-1 grid center, southwest of Mado-1ho), local water depth ~13.2-14.2m per nearby KHOA bathymetry points (vs ~8.5-9.4m for District II) -- a different, much deeper site. Report text (2021_taean_mado_report_extracted_text.txt lines 1169-1183): 18-1 excavated to 40x20m (extended east/west 10m each from an initial 20x20m grid), soil layered 0-60cm plain soft mud / 60-80cm shell-bearing soft mud / 80-100cm more viscous soft mud; a single ~150x50x30cm hull-bottom-plank fragment found at 40cm depth, plus 5 celadon dish fragments and 74 coal fragments scattered nearby (not modeled as separate objects -- too small/numerous for a legible mesh, and the report gives no individual coordinates for them). 18-2 (20x20m, relative position to 18-1 not given in report, approximated adjacent) had soil layered 0-60cm soft mud / 60-100cm more viscous soft mud and NO artifacts or hull evidence at all. Since SSS only images the surface layer and both blocks' top layer is described identically (plain soft mud, no shell/gravel contrast), there is no report-evidenced surface material contrast to represent as facies zones -- this environment is a single uniform soft-mud baseline, unlike District II's 8-zone patchwork. Per the excavation-report artifact catalog (line 6045), all 16 anchor stones and other stone artifacts came from District II, not here -- so anchor_stones is empty, not an omission. No reef-edge evidence for this site either. Terrain is real KHOA bathymetry (crop centered near the 18-1 grid, recentered so local (0,0) = the crop center, not the exact excavation point -- KHOA's ~150m point spacing means sub-100m precision isn't meaningful anyway).

baseline_material.comment: Very Fine Silt, Mz 7.5 Hamilton row -- same texture class already used for District II's soft_mud_baseline_material, reused here because the report's surface-layer description (무른 개흥층, plain soft mud) matches. Not claiming an independently-derived value for this specific site; APL-UW TR9407 Table 2 numbers are the same regardless of which site cites the row.

soft_mud_baseline_material.comment: Intentionally identical to baseline_material -- the site is uniform soft mud with no report-evidenced surface contrast, so the active-window blend below is inert by construction (both endpoints are the same value).

active_window.comment: Inert: baseline and soft_mud_baseline are identical, so this window has no visible effect. Left in place only because the JSON schema expects it.

texture_noise.comment: Generic micro-texture parameters, not site-specific evidence -- reused from mado_report_environment_v1 as reasonable defaults.

wreck_spawns.evidence: report line 1172-1176: bottom-plank (저판재) fragment, approx 150x50x30cm, found in 18-1 grid cell '2-1' at ~40cm depth below the seabed surface. This is a small fragment, not a full hull -- placed near the crop's local origin, offset 5m off the y=0 axis purely so a y=0 test survey track doesn't put it exactly on the sensor's nadir dead-zone for the entire pass (see top-level comment on why exact grid-cell position isn't recoverable to better than the ~150m KHOA point spacing anyway). burial_fraction=1.0 (max the schema supports) is a qualitative 'heavily buried' choice, not a calculation from the reported 40cm depth -- the BaseZ formula (terrain_z + 0.05 - burial_fraction*height) does not have a mode for 'buried N cm below current grade', only proud-to-flush, so 1.0 is the closest available representation, not a precise match to 40cm.
